extracted.intended_audience: MIT researchers / PIs and research administrators preparing grant proposals to federal agencies (DARPA, DOE, NSF) and foundations
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance and checklist for preparing competitive MIT grant proposals across DARPA, DOE, NSF, and foundation mechanisms, including required sections, institutional compliance, timelines, and voice/style expectations. Emphasizes MIT-specific resources, pre-submission checks by Research Administration Services (RAS), and funder-specific conventions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Heilmeier Catechism
rubrics_metrics.description: A set of questions to articulate the project concisely and non‑technically (used especially for DARPA proposals).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: What are you trying to do? Articulate without jargon. How is it done today, and what are the limits? What is new in your approach and why will it succeed? Who cares? If you succeed, what difference will it make? What are the risks? How much will it cost? How long will it take? What are the mid-term and final exams? (MIT teaches and expects proposals to address these explicitly.)

rubrics_metrics.name: DARPA: Statement of Work (SOW) with detailed milestones
rubrics_metrics.description: Include an explicit SOW that breaks the project into phases and deliverables with measurable milestones.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: SOW should include phase structure, concrete milestones, and measurable success criteria to support go/no-go decisions. Tie milestones to performance metrics and periodic decision points.

rubrics_metrics.name: DARPA: Quad chart (1‑page visual summary)
rubrics_metrics.description: Provide a one‑page quad chart summarizing the project for quick program officer and reviewer evaluation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Quad chart should concisely show objectives, approach, metrics, schedule, and impact in a visually accessible format.

rubrics_metrics.name: DARPA: Phase structure with go/no‑go decisions
rubrics_metrics.description: Design project with distinct phases and explicit go/no‑go criteria at decision points.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Define quantitative criteria for progression between phases; include contingency plans and risk mitigation tied to each decision gate.

rubrics_metrics.name: DARPA / DoD: IP and data rights considerations
rubrics_metrics.description: Address government purpose rights vs. unlimited rights and other IP/data rights up front.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explicitly state expected rights position, plan for commercialization/IP management, and any MIT/DoD/contractual constraints to avoid post-award negotiation delays.

rubrics_metrics.name: DARPA: Cost and schedule realism
rubrics_metrics.description: Budgets and schedules must be realistic and defensible for DARPA/DoD mechanisms.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide cost realism justification, realistic schedule with phase milestones, and alignment between tasks, personnel effort, and budget lines.

rubrics_metrics.name: What Wins DARPA (evaluation priorities)
rubrics_metrics.description: Features that increase competitiveness for DARPA proposals.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Bold technical vision; quantifiable performance metrics; explicit acknowledgement of risk with mitigation plans; inclusion of industry partners when appropriate; phase milestones with measurable success criteria.

rubrics_metrics.name: NSF: Project Description conventions and limits
rubrics_metrics.description: NSF proposals follow tight page limits and have specific review axes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Adhere to 15-page Project Description (very tight). Address Intellectual Merit and Broader Impacts equally. Make industry collaboration add concrete value in engineering/CS proposals. Education/outreach plans must be specific and tied to identifiable activities/programs.

rubrics_metrics.name: NSF: Intellectual Merit and Broader Impacts (equal weight)
rubrics_metrics.description: Proposals must clearly and separately address both Intellectual Merit and Broader Impacts.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Treat both sections substantively — do not relegate Broader Impacts to boilerplate. Tie Broader Impacts to specific programs, evaluation, and outcomes.

rubrics_metrics.name: NSF Center Grants (ERC, STC) expectations
rubrics_metrics.description: Center-scale proposals require multi-investigator and multi-institution scope plus additional institutional and industrial engagement.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Expect multi-institutional teams, required industry membership (for ERC), education at all levels (K‑12 through graduate), substantive diversity and inclusion plans, and a strategic vision for roughly a 10‑year horizon.

rubrics_metrics.name: DOE Office of Science conventions
rubrics_metrics.description: DOE-funded work should be mission-oriented and often leverages national lab partnerships and user facilities.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Emphasize mission relevance (energy, materials, basic science), value national lab partnerships, document planned use of user facilities (synchrotrons, supercomputers), and present a long-term research strategy.

rubrics_metrics.name: DOE Early Career Research Program eligibility and expectations
rubrics_metrics.description: Specific eligibility and award structure for DOE early career awards.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Typically within 10 years of PhD; 5‑year award (~$750K total); single PI; proposal should be mission-relevant and include research plan, biographical sketch, and budget aligned to DOE expectations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Bold technical vision with measurable success criteria
rubrics_metrics.description: Proposals should present an ambitious but specified technical vision and how success will be measured.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: State quantitative success criteria and measurable performance metrics. Avoid vague claims; link vision to milestones and measurable outcomes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Industry / national lab partnerships (where relevant)
rubrics_metrics.description: Demonstrate appropriate external partnerships to strengthen applied and mission‑oriented proposals.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Document roles, commitments, and value-add of industry or national lab partners. For some mechanisms (e.g., DARPA, ERC) industry involvement is expected or adds weight.

rubrics_metrics.name: Quantitative preliminary data
rubrics_metrics.description: Provide quantitative evidence that the approach is feasible and promising.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include pilot results, benchmarks, or other quantitative demonstrations that support feasibility and justify proposed milestones/metrics.

rubrics_metrics.name: Specific milestones with go/no‑go decisions
rubrics_metrics.description: Lay out concrete milestones tied to decisions and performance metrics.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Each milestone should have measurable criteria, timeline, and consequences (e.g., continue/stop/redirect). This is emphasized across DARPA/DoD and many mission agencies.

rubrics_metrics.name: Team composition that visibly covers all gaps
rubrics_metrics.description: Assemble a team whose combined expertise addresses all technical and managerial needs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Show how each team member's expertise fills a gap; include plans for missing capabilities (e.g., subcontract, consultant). Explicitly address leadership and project management roles.

rubrics_metrics.name: Cite MIT-specific resources and facilities
rubrics_metrics.description: Leverage and cite MIT cores, centers, and facilities to strengthen feasibility and capabilities claims.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Name relevant MIT resources (e.g., MIT.nano, Lincoln Laboratory, Plasma Science and Fusion Center, RLE, McGovern Institute, Broad Institute) and describe how they will be used and supported.

rubrics_metrics.name: Specific education/outreach plans
rubrics_metrics.description: Lay out concrete, implementable education and outreach activities tied to MIT programs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Describe targeted activities, audiences (K‑12, undergrad, grad), measurable outcomes, partnerships, and evaluation plans rather than vague statements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Substantive diversity and inclusion plans
rubrics_metrics.description: Provide meaningful plans to promote diversity, equity, and inclusion as part of the project.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Avoid boilerplate; include recruitment, retention, mentoring, evaluation metrics, and ties to MIT or external programs to show impact.

rubrics_metrics.name: Realistic budget aligned with MIT indirect costs
rubrics_metrics.description: Budgets must be realistic and properly incorporate MIT's indirect cost rates and institutional policies.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure effort, direct costs, and F&A calculations are consistent with MIT rates. Provide justification for major cost items and explain any cost share.

rubrics_metrics.name: Risk acknowledged with mitigation
rubrics_metrics.description: Explicitly acknowledge technical and programmatic risks and provide mitigation strategies.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not hide risks; present contingency plans, alternative approaches, and how risk reduction will be measured over milestones.

rubrics_metrics.name: Pre‑submission cost realism checks
rubrics_metrics.description: MIT RAS will check for unrealistic costs or mismatches between scope and budget.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Confirm that budgets map to tasks and effort, and include justifications to withstand institutional and agency review.

rubrics_metrics.name: Compliance gap checks (export control, ITAR)
rubrics_metrics.description: Identify and resolve compliance issues before submission (e.g., export controls, ITAR).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Flag any work with restricted technologies or foreign collaborations early; consult MIT compliance offices and build any required controls into plans and budgets.

rubrics_metrics.name: IP and data rights review
rubrics_metrics.description: Resolve intellectual property and data rights positions before proposal submission, especially for DoD/DARPA work.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Work with Tech Licensing and RAS to state expected rights, data sharing plans, and any constraints that could affect award negotiations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Budget accuracy checks (effort, indirect calculations)
rubrics_metrics.description: Ensure accuracy in personnel effort reporting and indirect cost calculations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: RAS will look for typical budget errors; validate effort allocations, fringe, and F&A computations against MIT policies prior to submission.

rubrics_metrics.name: Format and section completeness
rubrics_metrics.description: Follow funder format rules and include all required sections (especially DoD-specific sections).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Avoid format violations; include any agency-specific attachments/clauses. MIT RAS flags missing sections prior to submission.

rubrics_metrics.name: Cite industry liaison and institute programs where relevant
rubrics_metrics.description: Reference MIT programs that demonstrate industry engagement and translational pathways.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Mention MIT Industrial Liaison Program, MIT Energy Initiative, consortia, or industry-sponsored research pathways to show engagement and impact potential.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use RAS pre‑award services
rubrics_metrics.description: Engage Research Administration Services for budget development, subcontract negotiation, compliance review, cost share analysis, and submission.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: RAS offers budget development, subcontract negotiation, compliance review, cost share analysis, and submission via the MIT Coeus system — involve them early for institutional alignment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Pre‑submission timeline requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: Internal MIT timeline for proposal preparation and RAS reviews.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Begin budget and admin docs 4–6 weeks before the deadline; provide a full draft 2 weeks before for compliance review; allow 1 week for final formatting and submission. Adhere to these windows to ensure institutional review.

rubrics_metrics.name: Engineering / DARPA voice and style
rubrics_metrics.description: Tone and style conventions for engineering and mission-oriented proposals.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prefer quantitative claims with explicit metrics, an optimistic but risk‑aware tone, highlighted industry partnerships, clearly specified performance benchmarks, and a schedule with concrete milestones. Avoid vague language and emphasize measurable outcomes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Academic / NSF voice and style
rubrics_metrics.description: Tone and style conventions for NSF and academic proposals.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Be expansive about intellectual merit while making Broader Impacts concrete. Tie education plans to MIT programs, make diversity plans substantive, and provide scholarly context and rigor appropriate to peer review.
